image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a rocky substrate. The organism has an elongated oval shape with a distinct dorsal armor consisting of eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in a linear series. The plates are yellowish-green with brownish mottling and visible growth lines. Surrounding the plates is a thick, leathery girdle covered in fine, hair-like spines (setae). The background consists of dark, textured rock with some encrusting algae or marine growth.
